lines: Envelope generator making an AD envelope from a trigger and an ASR envelope from a gate, with stage gate outputs, looping modes and wide voltage control of stage times
Sets the range of both time knobs: slow 0.044 to 181 seconds, medium 0.0028 to 11.3 seconds, fast 0.00024 to 1.0 seconds, or glacial 0.707 seconds to 48.27 minutes
Picks the retrigger and looping behaviour: retrigger from the current level, retrigger from 0, a loop started and stopped by TRIG, or an AD envelope that loops while GATE is high
Makes the GATE button a toggle, one press taking the gate high and the next taking it low, in place of a gate that lasts while the button is held
Fires an AD envelope by hand, held high for as long as the button is pressed
Raises the gate by hand for an ASR envelope, held high for as long as the button is pressed
Sets the curve of that stage, concave counter-clockwise, linear at noon and convex clockwise, with no change to the stage time
Sets the base length of that stage, within the range picked by SPD
Attenuates and inverts the CV input for that stage time, and at -100% a pitch voltage fed to both CV inputs makes a looping envelope track a volt per octave
Every positive volt here doubles the length of that stage and every negative volt halves it, after the attenuverter for that stage
A rising edge starts an AD envelope; it reads high above 2V and low below 0.2V
A high gate starts an ASR envelope, which holds 10V while the gate stays high; it reads high above 2V and low below 0.2V
Carries a 10V gate while the envelope is rising, or a 1ms trigger at the start or end of the rise
Chooses what the RISE output carries: a gate while rising, a 1ms trigger on entering the rise, or a 1ms trigger on leaving it
Carries a 10V gate while the envelope is falling, or a 1ms trigger at the start or end of the fall, or when it reaches 0V
Chooses what the FALL output carries: a gate while falling, a trigger on entering the fall, a trigger on leaving it, or an end-of-cycle trigger at 0V
Carries a 10V gate while the envelope holds at 10V, or a 1ms trigger at the start or end of that sustain
Chooses what the SUS output carries: a gate while sustaining, a 1ms trigger on entering the sustain, or a 1ms trigger on leaving it
The envelope itself, 0-10V unless the ENV mode button inverts it or shifts it to bipolar
Sets the range of the ENV output: 0-10V, inverted from 10V down to 0V, or bipolar from -5V to 5V
Note — patching a stage gate output back into TRIG or GATE blocks retriggering during that stage, and patching the RISE gate into GATE makes an ASR attack always climb to full
Auxilliary Clone Expander: adds four more cloned polyphonic input and output pairs to a Clone Merge, Poly Clone or Poly Unison, and goes immediately to the right of it
Sets the channel order at the output of the same number: yellow keeps all the copies of one input channel together, blue lays out the input channels as a set and repeats the whole set
A polyphonic signal copied by the parent module's clone count and carried to the output of the same number; unpatched it counts as one channel of 0V
Carries the input of the same number copied to the parent's channel count; its lamp is yellow when every channel copied, orange when missing ones were filled with 0V, red when extra ones were dropped
Note — with a Poly Unison as the parent these outputs are copied but not detuned, and a lamp glows yellow while the module is connected to a parent
Bay Input: a transmitter that carries eight polyphonic signals to Bay Output and Bay Norm modules anywhere in the patch, with no cable and no sample delay
One of eight signals carried to every Bay Output and Bay Norm linked to this module; a name given to the port in its context menu appears as a label above it
Menu — the module name set here appears as a label at the top of the panel and identifies this module in the source list of every Bay Output and Bay Norm; changing it later does not break a link
Bay Norm: a receiver that carries the eight signals of one Bay Input module anywhere in the patch, falling back to its own input where the source is unpatched
Feeds the output of the same number whenever the port of the same number on the linked Bay Input is unpatched, or no source is linked
Carries the port of the same number on the linked Bay Input, or its own normal input when that source port is unpatched
Menu — Output source picks which Bay Input this module receives from; Enable 0 Channel output gives a port with no source and no normal a cable of no channels, which a destination treats as no cable
Bay Output: a receiver that carries the eight signals of one Bay Input module anywhere in the patch, with no cable and no sample delay
Carries the port of the same number on the linked Bay Input; monophonic 0V while no source is linked or that source port is unpatched
Menu — Output source picks which Bay Input this module receives from; Enable 0 Channel output gives an unlinked or unpatched port a cable of no channels, which a destination treats as no cable
A chaotic Benjolin oscillator: two cross-modulating oscillators feeding a rungler shift register, with triangle, pulse, comparator and stepped voltage outputs
Sets the base frequency of oscillator one, about 0.03Hz fully anticlockwise, about 15Hz at noon and about 7800Hz fully clockwise; modulation can drive it to about 12500Hz
Sets the base frequency of oscillator two, about 0.03Hz fully anticlockwise, about 15Hz at noon and about 7800Hz fully clockwise; modulation can drive it to about 12500Hz
An attenuverter, -1 to +1, setting how far the rungler stepped voltage modulates the frequency of oscillator one; noon gives no modulation
An attenuverter, -1 to +1, setting how far the rungler stepped voltage modulates the frequency of oscillator two; noon gives no modulation
An attenuverter, -1 to +1, setting how far the CV1 input modulates the frequency of oscillator one; noon gives no modulation
An attenuverter, -1 to +1, setting how far the CV2 input modulates the frequency of oscillator two; noon gives no modulation
Picks the oversample rate applied to the outputs: off, x2, x4, x8, x16 or x32, with x8 the default; more oversampling cuts aliasing on high frequency output and costs CPU
Fully anticlockwise the rungler runs an 8 step pattern, fully clockwise a 16 step pattern whose halves mirror each other, and at noon the output is chaotic
Ignores the PATTERN knob and runs the shift register as a 127 step linear feedback register, so the rungler output stays chaotic; each press toggles it
Clocks the rungler on both edges of the clock gate rather than the leading edge alone, so it steps at double the rate; each press toggles it
Bipolar voltage modulating the frequency of oscillator one through the CV1 knob; with nothing patched here the TRI2 output is normalled in
Bipolar voltage modulating the frequency of oscillator two through the CV2 knob; with nothing patched here the TRI1 output is normalled in
A rising edge above 2V toggles the CHAOS button
A rising edge above 2V toggles the DOUBLE button
Clocks the rungler shift register, reading high above 1V and low below -1V; with nothing patched here the PULSE2 output is normalled in
The triangle wave of oscillator one, swinging between -5V and 5V
The triangle wave of oscillator two, swinging between -5V and 5V
The pulse wave of oscillator one, -5V low and 5V high
The pulse wave of oscillator two, -5V low and 5V high
The first bit of the rungler shift register, -5V when low and 5V when high
5V whenever the TRI2 signal is above the TRI1 signal and -5V otherwise, giving a pulse of varying width; this is the output a Benjolin feeds to its filter
The rungler stepped voltage, eight possible levels between -5V and 5V, changing each time the rungler is clocked
Note — the eight LEDs above the RUNGLER label show the shift register bits, with the three bits feeding the converter lit brighter than the rest
Menu — the rungler converter reads bits 2,4,7 by default, which gives the most patterns; switching it to bits 6,7,8 gives Rob Hordijk's original design
Menu — Unipolar clock input reads the CLOCK input against 0.1V instead of -1V, which is what a clock that never goes negative needs
Menu — Original release normalled values scales the normalled CV and clock signals to a fifth of their voltage, for patches built before that was corrected
Menu — the oversampling filter is 10th order with a cutoff at 80% of Nyquist by default, with 8th order at 80% and 6th order at 50% also offered
Expands the Benjolin Oscillator with eight rungler gate outputs; place it immediately to the right of the oscillator, or in an unbroken chain of expanders running right from it
Shapes every gate output: a gate while the logic is true, that gate only while the rungler clock is high or only while low, or a 1ms trigger as the logic goes true, on a clock rise, fall or edge
Picks the gate voltages: unipolar, 0V low and 10V high, or bipolar, -5V low and 5V high
A gate driven by the rungler bits picked in its right-click menu and combined with AND, OR or XOR; by default it follows the single bit matching its number, and the label above shows the logic
Note — the gate outputs are computed at the sample rate, so oversampling on the Benjolin Oscillator does not reach them
Menu — four factory presets fill all eight ports at once: one gate per rungler bit, or AND, OR or XOR combinations of bits
Expands the Benjolin Oscillator with a rungler CV output you weight bit by bit; place it immediately to the right of the oscillator, or in an unbroken chain of expanders running right from it
On, the bit knobs snap to 0, 1, 2, 4 and so on to 128; off, they take any value in between
Sets the weight this rungler bit contributes, 0 to 128; the weights of the bits that are high are summed and divided by the total of all eight, so a bit set to 0 drops out of the conversion
Scales the peak to peak swing of the output, 0-10V, centred on 0V before the offset is added; the default is 10V
Shifts the output by -10V to 10V, applied after the range
The converted rungler voltage, stepping each time the rungler is clocked
Note — the output is computed at the sample rate, so oversampling on the Benjolin Oscillator does not reach it
Stochastically routes two inputs to two outputs, a virtual coin toss at each trigger deciding whether they swap
Sets the chance of the routing operation, 0% fully anticlockwise and 100% fully clockwise, with 50% at noon
Adds 10V to the TRIG input, which fires a coin toss whenever that crosses the rise threshold
Picks what a positive coin toss does: TOG flips the current routing, SWAP sets the swapped routing, GATE holds a swap while TRIG is low and allows no-swap for the length of a high TRIG
Sets the voltage the trigger must rise to before it counts as high, -10V to 10V, 1V by default
Sets the voltage the trigger must fall below before it counts as low again, -10V to 10V, 0.1V by default
Adds an offset of -10V to 10V to that input, applied after its SCALE knob
Attenuates or inverts that input, -1 to 1, before its OFFSET knob is added
One of the two signals the coin toss routes; unpatched it takes the TRIG input
The other signal the coin toss routes; unpatched it is 0V
Carries the A input while the routing is unswapped and the B input while it is swapped
Carries the B input while the routing is unswapped and the A input while it is swapped
A rise past the RISE threshold fires a coin toss; the input counts as low again once it drops below the FALL threshold
Modulates the probability, each volt adding 10% of chance to the PROB knob
Picks what the A input is normalled to: red passes the raw trigger input, blue passes the Schmitt trigger gate, 0V low and 10V high
Note — setting RISE below FALL reverses the trigger, so the coin toss happens on the falling edge instead
Menu — coin flips are counted from the TRIG and PROB channels by default, or from all four inputs, which lets A and B channels scramble across the two outputs
Menu — Audio Process adds an antipop crossfade for slow switching or oversampling for switching at audio rates; leave it off for gates and CV
Menu — Monitor Channel picks which polyphonic channel the two routing lights report, or turns them off
Adds a CV input for every Bernoulli Switch parameter; place it immediately to the right of a Bernoulli Switch
Sets the routing mode and overrides the switch on the Bernoulli Switch while patched: -1V and below is TOGGLE, between -1V and 1V is SWAP, 1V and above is GATE
Attenuates the signal at the Bernoulli Switch PROB input, -1 to 1
Attenuates its own CV input, -1 to 1, before that CV is added to the matching Bernoulli Switch knob
Shifts the Bernoulli Switch rise threshold, its attenuated voltage added to the RISE knob
Shifts the Bernoulli Switch fall threshold, its attenuated voltage added to the FALL knob
Shifts the offset applied to the Bernoulli Switch A input, its attenuated voltage added to the A OFFSET knob
Shifts the offset applied to the Bernoulli Switch B input, its attenuated voltage added to the B OFFSET knob
Shifts the scaling of the Bernoulli Switch A input, 10V of attenuated CV moving the A SCALE value by 1
Shifts the scaling of the Bernoulli Switch B input, 10V of attenuated CV moving the B SCALE value by 1
Note — every input here is monophonic and is applied equally to all channels at the Bernoulli Switch, and none of them are oversampled
Blocker: a 1HP module that breaks the run of neighbours Venom Bypass and Stoermelder Strip work along, so they stop at it. It blocks while bypassed too, and doubles as a near-free blank
Bypass: bypasses the modules at the far ends of its cables, by button or by CV
Pressing it turns the bypass state on or off and it glows red while that state is on; with momentary mode set, it inverts the state only while it is held
Sets what the trigger button does: dark, each press toggles the bypass state; yellow, a press inverts the bypass state only while the button is held
Sets what the trigger input does: dark, a rising edge toggles the bypass state; green, a high gate turns the bypass on and a low gate turns it off; red, that gate is inverted
A trigger or gate that changes the bypass state, read as a Schmitt trigger going high at 2V and low at 0.1V; the G button sets which of the two it is
Passes every channel patched here through to the output it is paired with, and is the route by which the source module is bypassed
Sets which modules at the source end of the cable patched into its input are bypassed: none, the source alone, or the source with its unbroken neighbours to the left, to the right, or both ways
Carries the channels of the input it is paired with; while that input is unpatched the cable here has no channels, which the destination treats as no cable and so keeps its own normalled value
Sets which modules at the far end of the cable patched into its output are bypassed: none, the target alone, or the target with its unbroken neighbours to the left, to the right, or both ways
Note — a run of neighbours ends at a gap, at another Bypass module, or at a Venom Blocker, and none of those three is included in it
Clone Merge: copies each of up to eight monophonic inputs a chosen number of times and merges every copy into one polyphonic output
Sets how many copies are made of each input, from 1 to 16
One monophonic signal to be copied; patch these from the top down. Its lamp is yellow while its copies fit within 16 channels and red when they do not, and an input that does not fit is left out
Sets the channel order at the output: yellow keeps all the copies of one input together, blue lays out the inputs as a set and repeats the whole set
Every copy of every input merged into one polyphonic cable, in the order the GRP button sets
Menu — an Auxilliary Clone Expander can be added from here, which gives four more polyphonic input and output pairs copied by the same count
Eight inputs placed at the corners of a cube and crossfaded into one output, with X, Y and Z faders blending between opposite faces
Sets the left to right blend, read as percent right, with 50% at the centre of its travel
Sets the bottom to top blend, read as percent top, with 50% at the centre of its travel
Sets the front to back blend, read as percent back, with 50% at the centre of its travel
Attenuates and inverts the X CV before it is added to the X fader
Attenuates and inverts the Y CV before it is added to the Y fader
Attenuates and inverts the Z CV before it is added to the Z fader
Turned on, the polyphonic channels of the output are summed into one monophonic signal
Attenuates the final output between 0% and 100%, at 100% by default
Bipolar CV added to the X fader through its attenuator, scaled at 10% per volt, with the sum clamped between 0% and 100%
Bipolar CV added to the Y fader through its attenuator, scaled at 10% per volt, with the sum clamped between 0% and 100%
Bipolar CV added to the Z fader through its attenuator, scaled at 10% per volt, with the sum clamped between 0% and 100%
The cube's bottom left front corner; patched with all seven other corners empty, its polyphonic channels are read as the eight corners in turn, this one first
The cube's bottom right front corner, blended into the output by the X, Y and Z faders
The cube's top left front corner, blended into the output by the X, Y and Z faders
The cube's top right front corner, blended into the output by the X, Y and Z faders
The cube's bottom left back corner, blended into the output by the X, Y and Z faders
The cube's bottom right back corner, blended into the output by the X, Y and Z faders
The cube's top left back corner, blended into the output by the X, Y and Z faders
The cube's top right back corner, blended into the output by the X, Y and Z faders
The blend of the eight corner inputs after the output level; with every fader at an extreme one corner makes up all of it, and with all three at 50% each corner contributes 12.5%
Menu — CV amount scale runs -100% to 100% by default, or -200% to 200%, which lets a bipolar 5V sine or triangle drive a dimension to one extreme and hold there
Builds a harmonic or subharmonic partial above a root pitch, or quantizes an incoming pitch to the nearest partial of that root
Picks which partials are available: A for all of them, O for odd ones, E for even ones plus the fundamental
Selects the partial number, 1 being the fundamental and 16 four octaves above it; negative numbers give subharmonics
Attenuates and inverts the CV input before it shifts the partial number
Shifts the selected partial by one for every 0.1V, clamped to the active partial range
Detunes the output away from the exact partial, none at noon, flat to the left and sharp to the right
Sets how much the detune shrinks as pitch rises; fully counter-clockwise holds the detune constant, fully clockwise halves it every octave so the beat rate stays even, and that is where it starts
The fundamental pitch that the partials are counted from, the first partial
A pitch patched here is quantized to the nearest partial or subharmonic of ROOT, within seven octaves either way, and the Partial and CV controls are then ignored
The chosen partial as a pitch, the root plus the interval of that partial
Menu — Partial Range sets the span of the Partial knob, from 1 to 16 by default and out to 128 partials above, below, or both
Menu — Monitor channel picks which polyphonic channel the numeric display reads, channel 1 by default
Knob 5: five knobs, each putting out a constant voltage on its own jack
Sets the constant voltage at the output of the same number, covering -10V to 10V until its own menu is told otherwise
Carries the constant voltage of the knob of the same number, monophonic unless that knob's menu sets more channels
Menu — a knob's own menu sets its range, from 0-1V up to a custom pair of end values, quantizes it to octaves or semitones, and sets how many identical channels its output carries
Linear Beats: lets only one trigger strike at a time across nine channels of gates, turning coincident drum triggers into a linear pattern

Sets how that channel behaves: green blocks its gate when a channel above goes high at that moment, dark passes every gate, orange blocks coincident gates but not those below, white starts a new group
Gates for that lettered channel, read as Schmitt triggers going high at 1V and low at 0.1V. A takes precedence over B and so on, and within a polyphonic cable the lower numbered channels do
Gates are looked at only on a rising edge here, which lines up inputs that are not sample-accurate. Delay it at least as much as the latest input, and run it at twice the fastest channel
Carries the gates of its lettered channel that were not blocked, 10V high and 0V low
Menu — Expander CV toggles button on/off sets what a Linear Beats Expander's CV inputs do: off, a high gate mutes and a low gate unmutes; on, each rising edge flips the mute instead
Linear Beats Expander: adds mutes and a disable switch to a Linear Beats module, immediately to its left or its right. On the left it mutes the inputs, on the right the outputs
Red mutes that lettered channel of the Linear Beats, and each press flips it
A gate that mutes that lettered channel: high mutes and low unmutes, unless Expander CV toggles button on/off is set on the Linear Beats, when each rising edge flips the mute instead
Red turns off linear drumming on the Linear Beats, so every incoming trigger passes through with nothing synced to a clock; the mutes on this expander go on working
A gate that turns off linear drumming: high disables and low restores it, unless Expander CV toggles button on/off is set on the Linear Beats, when each rising edge flips it instead
Note — an input mute stops its channel blocking lower channels, while an output mute lets it go on blocking. A lamp glows yellow on the side the Linear Beats was found
Nine polyphonic logic gates, each combining its own inputs with any of the standard logic operations
Off gives every polyphonic channel its own gate; on collects the channels of an input as separate inputs to one monophonic gate
Sets oversampling to off, 2x, 4x, 8x, 16x or 32x, cutting aliasing when the outputs are used as audio; off costs the least CPU
Sets the low and high output voltages: 0-1V, 0-5V or 0-10V for CV work, or the bipolar 1V, 5V and 10V pairs for audio
Removes DC offset from the outputs, which matters when they are used as audio
Sets the voltage an input must rise above to count as high, summed with the HIGH THRESH input; -10V to 10V, 2V by default
Sets the voltage an input must fall to before it counts as low, summed with the LOW THRESH input; -10V to 10V, 0.1V by default
Shifts the high threshold used by every input, added to the HIGH THRESH knob
Shifts the low threshold used by every input, added to the LOW THRESH knob
One of the two gate inputs for that row, ignored while unpatched
Picks an output from a row above to include as an extra input to this row without a sample delay; three dashes takes none
Fixed at three dashes, because there is no row above whose output could be reused
Sets the logic for that row: AND, OR, XOR 1, XOR ODD, NAND, NOR, XNOR 1, XNOR ODD, or defer, which passes the row's inputs down to the row below
Carries the result of that row's logic operation, and constant 0V when the row is deferred or has no inputs
Note — with a single input AND, OR, XOR 1 and XOR ODD pass it through, while NAND, NOR, XNOR 1 and XNOR ODD invert it
Note — the two thresholds are swapped internally whenever the high threshold is set below the low one
Menu — the oversampling filter runs at 10th order by default, with 8th and 6th order options that cost less CPU and pass less high frequency content
Merge 4x2: two independent sections, each merging up to four monophonic or polyphonic inputs into one polyphonic output
One of the signals merged into its section's output. Patch a section from the top down; a gap above the last patched port counts as one channel of 0V, and the lamp glows red when channels did not fit
The four inputs of the upper section merged into one polyphonic cable. Left unpatched, those four inputs are passed down to the lower output instead, so all eight can be merged into one cable
The four inputs of the lower section merged into one polyphonic cable, together with the upper four when the upper output is unpatched
Merge Split: a merge section combining up to four inputs into one polyphonic output, and beneath it a split section breaking one polyphonic input back out across four outputs
One of the four signals merged into the merge output; the lamp beside it glows red when its channels did not fit within the 16 that output can carry
The four merge inputs combined into one polyphonic cable of at most 16 channels
The polyphonic signal broken out across the four split outputs
Carries part of the split input. When that input has as many channels as the merge section took in, it matches the merge input of the same number and a lamp glows yellow; otherwise it is monophonic
Menu — a split output's channel count can be fixed in its own port menu, which stops it following the merge section; a module menu option puts all four back to following it
Four-channel polyphonic mixer for audio or CV, with a level knob per input and options to clip the mix or strip DC from it
Attenuates, inverts or amplifies that numbered input before it reaches the mix; the M button sets what the knob's range means
Attenuates, inverts or amplifies the sum of the four channels; the M button sets what the knob's range means
Cycles five level scales: unipolar dB, unipolar dB with polyphonic inputs summed to mono, and bipolar percent, x2 and x10; under a bipolar scale an unpatched input becomes a constant voltage
Cycles DC offset removal through off, before clipping, before and after clipping, and after clipping
Cycles eight clipping settings for the mix: off, hard or soft at 10V taken before or after the mix level, oversampled soft versions of those, and a saturate at 6V
One of the four channel inputs, scaled by its level knob; left unpatched under a bipolar level mode it becomes a constant voltage that the knob sets
The four scaled inputs summed, then passed through the mix level knob, the clipping and the DC blocking; it carries as many polyphonic channels as the busiest input
Note — mix expanders added in an unbroken chain to the right bring mute, solo, fade, pan, offset and send controls to the four channels
Menu — oversampling filter quality sets how hard the module works to suppress aliasing in the oversampled soft clipping settings
Four-channel polyphonic stereo mixer for audio or CV, one level knob per stereo pair, with options to clip the mix or strip DC from it
Attenuates, inverts or amplifies both sides of that numbered stereo input before the mix; the MODE button sets what the knob's range means
Attenuates, inverts or amplifies the stereo mix; the MODE button sets what the knob's range means
Cycles five level scales: unipolar dB, unipolar dB with polyphonic inputs summed to mono, and bipolar percent, x2 and x10; a bipolar scale gives constant CV only when both sides are unpatched
Cycles DC offset removal through off, before clipping, before and after clipping, and after clipping
Cycles eight clipping settings for the mix: off, hard or soft at 10V taken before or after the mix level, oversampled soft versions of those, and a saturate at 6V
The left side of that numbered stereo input; patched on its own it feeds both sides, because the right input is normalled to it
The right side of that numbered stereo input, normalled to the left input of the same pair
The left side of the mix, after the mix level knob, the clipping and the DC blocking; both mix outputs carry the same number of polyphonic channels
The right side of the mix, after the mix level knob, the clipping and the DC blocking; both mix outputs carry the same number of polyphonic channels
Note — mix expanders added in an unbroken chain to the right bring mute, solo, fade, pan, offset and send controls to the four channels
Menu — oversampling filter quality sets how hard the module works to suppress aliasing in the oversampled soft clipping settings
Expander for the MIX MUTE and MIX SOLO expanders, turning their mute and unmute switches into timed fades; it goes immediately to the right of a MIX MUTE or MIX SOLO expander
Sets how long that numbered channel takes to fade in and how long it takes to fade out, from 0 to 30 seconds
Sets how long the final mix takes to fade in and how long it takes to fade out, from 0 to 30 seconds
Curves that channel's fade: exponential at full counterclockwise, linear at noon, logarithmic at full clockwise, and a blend in between
Curves the fade of the final mix: exponential at full counterclockwise, linear at noon, logarithmic at full clockwise, and a blend in between
The fade level of that numbered channel as CV, 0V when it is fully muted and 10V when it is fully unmuted
The fade level of the final mix as CV, 0V when it is fully muted and 10V when it is fully unmuted
Note — the mute and unmute switching itself comes from a MIX MUTE or MIX SOLO expander; this module only times the transitions
Note — one fade expander can be used per mix module, and a MIX FADE 2 cannot be used alongside it
Note — the indicator lamp glows yellow once the expander has connected to a mix module
Expander for the MIX MUTE and MIX SOLO expanders, turning their mute and unmute switches into timed fades with separate rise and fall times; it goes immediately to the right of one of them
Sets how long that numbered channel takes to fade in, from 0 to 30 seconds
Sets how long that numbered channel takes to fade out, from 0 to 30 seconds
Sets how long the final mix takes to fade in, from 0 to 30 seconds
Sets how long the final mix takes to fade out, from 0 to 30 seconds
Curves that channel's fade: exponential at full counterclockwise, linear at noon, logarithmic at full clockwise, and a blend in between
Curves the fade of the final mix: exponential at full counterclockwise, linear at noon, logarithmic at full clockwise, and a blend in between
The fade level of that numbered channel as CV, 0V when it is fully muted and 10V when it is fully unmuted
The fade level of the final mix as CV, 0V when it is fully muted and 10V when it is fully unmuted
Note — the mute and unmute switching itself comes from a MIX MUTE or MIX SOLO expander; this module only times the transitions
Note — one fade expander can be used per mix module, and a MIX FADE cannot be used alongside it
Note — the indicator lamp glows yellow once the expander has connected to a mix module
Expander for MIX 4, MIX 4 STEREO, VCA MIX 4 and VCA MIX 4 STEREO, muting numbered channels or the whole mix; it goes to the right of the mix module, in the chain of expanders there
Mutes that numbered channel while the button glows bright red; a lit button on a MIX SOLO expander overrides it
Mutes the final mix while the button glows bright red
Mutes that numbered channel when the voltage rises to 1V or more, and unmutes it when the voltage falls to 0.1V or less
Mutes the final mix when the voltage rises to 1V or more, and unmutes it when the voltage falls to 0.1V or less
Note — a button press always toggles the mute state, so it overrides what the CV input has set
Note — one mute expander can be used per mix module, and it must be adjacent to a MIX SOLO expander if one is used
Note — the indicator lamp glows yellow once the expander has connected to a mix module
Menu — Mute/solo CV toggles on/off, on the mix module, makes the CV inputs toggle the mute on each rise instead of acting as gates
Menu — Soft mute/solo, on the mix module, slews each mute transition over 25ms; switch it off for an immediate cut
Expander for MIX 4, MIX 4 STEREO, VCA MIX 4 and VCA MIX 4 STEREO, adding constant offset voltages around the level gains; it goes immediately to the right of the mix module
Adds a constant voltage between -10V and 10V to that numbered channel before its LEVEL knob is applied
Adds a constant voltage between -10V and 10V to the summed mix before the MIX level knob is applied
Adds a constant voltage between -10V and 10V to that numbered channel after its LEVEL knob is applied
Adds a constant voltage between -10V and 10V to the mix after the MIX level knob is applied
Note — these offsets appear in the numbered channel outputs of VCA MIX 4 and VCA MIX 4 STEREO, which the other mix expanders do not
